headline: TJX posted a 6% comp with sales up 9% and EPS up 29%, well above plan, and raised its full-year outlook.
guidance_note: FY27 comp raised to +3-4% (from 2-3%); EPS raised to $5.08-5.15 (from $4.93-5.02), assuming current fuel prices persist. Q2 comp +2-3%.
key_messages: Consolidated comp +6% (vs plan of 2-3%), driven equally by higher average basket and more customer transactions.
Marmaxx US comp +6%, HomeGoods +9%, TJX Canada +7%, TJX International +4%.
Gross margin +180 bps to 31.3% on merchandise margin, inventory/fuel hedges and expense leverage.
Herrman saw no change in customer behavior from macro factors; continues to attract disproportionate Gen Z and millennial shoppers.
Merchandise availability 'off the charts'; outlook held back partly on higher fuel cost assumptions.

consumer.income_split: Customer income mix balanced but somewhat higher than the general population, per management.
consumer.pricing: Higher fuel prices flagged as a margin headwind for the rest of the year.

macro_read: Broad comp and traffic gains in spring 2026 suggest value-oriented discretionary spending was solid; management reported no macro-driven change in behavior.
